directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Stark starts from an identity derived from the Hadamard factorization of a Dedekind zeta function, eliminates two difficult constants, uses the prime-ideal expansion for real s greater than 1, and specializes s near 1 to bound discriminants. Later work combines differentiated versions of the identity, while Guinand-Weil explicit formulas sharpen the method and support unconditional variants.
directed.conceptual_reading: The method replaces inaccessible constants by a decomposition whose prime and zero contributions can be estimated or discarded under explicit sign conditions. Its gain is not merely a stronger estimate: the explicit-formula form exposes which contributions and positivity requirements carry the proof burden.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Hadamard factorization and logarithmic-derivative identities bridge zeros and prime ideals to the discriminant; differentiated identities and explicit formulas are alternative representations that make cancellation and sign control available.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: If a field K has class number h, its Hilbert class field L has degree governed by h and the same root discriminant as K. If discriminant lower bounds force every nontrivial candidate L of the relevant degree to have root discriminant larger than that preserved value, then L=K and h=1. More generally, analytic bounds first give class-number upper bounds that algebraic methods can lower.
directed.conceptual_reading: An invariant-preserving lift turns an arithmetic quantity that is difficult to inspect directly into a forbidden extension-size problem. Root-discriminant invariance supplies the fixed value, and degree growth supplies the axis along which lower bounds become a contradiction certificate.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The Hilbert class field is the bridge object: it represents class number as extension degree while retaining root discriminant, connecting analytic discriminant estimates to algebraic class-group conclusions.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The argument certifies particular fields and does not resolve the contrasting heuristic expectation that class number one is frequent or the open question of whether infinitely many such fields exist.
directed.uncertainty: The degree display is OCR-damaged, so the exact equation should be recovered from the scan, but the invariance-and-contradiction mechanism is explicit in the prose.

A degree-nine polynomial gives a field of prime discriminant whose minimality is unknown. Known infinite-tower constructions use small-primary parts of class groups and produce composite prime-power degree patterns, leaving boundedness of d_p for prime p open.
